classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equal tangent pairs as four isosceles corner triangles, obtain the missing outer angle, and combine adjacent base angles along each straight side to determine the inner quadrilateral.

content.prompt: The circle touches the sides of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ at $P$, $Q$, $R$ and $S$ as shown. Find the angles of the quadrilateral $PQRS$.

spec.description: Circumscribed quadrilateral ABCD, circle centre O, tangent contacts P, Q, R, S and inscribed edges PQ, QR, RS, SP. Given angles at A and C have leader lines; the angle at D is labelled inside.
spec.mathematics: Tangency is coordinate-derived. Outer interior angles A = 110 degrees, C = 100 degrees and D = 60 degrees; vertex and contact-point order match the source.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the three given outer angles appear; no angles of PQRS are supplied.

answer.worked:
$AP = AS$, $BP = BQ$, $CQ = CR$ and $DR = DS$ because tangents from an external point are equal. The four corner triangles are therefore isosceles.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ABC &= 360^\circ-110^\circ-100^\circ-60^\circ=90^\circ\\\angle APS &= \frac{180^\circ-110^\circ}{2}=35^\circ\\\angle BPQ &= \frac{180^\circ-90^\circ}{2}=45^\circ\\\angle CQR &= \frac{180^\circ-100^\circ}{2}=40^\circ\\\angle DRS &= \frac{180^\circ-60^\circ}{2}=60^\circ\end{align*}$$
Using the equal base angles and angles on a straight line:
$$\begin{align*}\angle SPQ &= 180^\circ-35^\circ-45^\circ=100^\circ\\\angle PQR &= 180^\circ-45^\circ-40^\circ=95^\circ\\\angle QRS &= 180^\circ-40^\circ-60^\circ=80^\circ\\\angle RSP &= 180^\circ-60^\circ-35^\circ=85^\circ\end{align*}$$
